minutes.headline: Commissioners split over locking in state loan funding for the PFAS treatment plant ahead of a May resident vote
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District board spent most of this meeting refining a joint PowerPoint on funding options (SRF loan and bond) for a combined PFAS/iron-manganese treatment plant and transmission-main project, ahead of a special resident meeting set for late May. Commissioners disagreed sharply over whether to secure the full SRF loan amount now versus waiting for firmer design-stage cost numbers, with no vote taken on that question; the board also voted on a special-meeting date, amended shutoff/collections rules, and directed a letter to MassDEP over a condo association's kayak rack.

public_comment.topic: Suggested the board may need a separate vote to fund the treatment plant design even if the main SRF/bond vote fails, since design money would still be spent.
Raised concern about how large the total project cost and resulting water-bill increase would be for residents, especially with many accounts already behind on payments.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of April 8th and April 15th
Hold the special meeting on either May 27th or May 28th depending on school-space availability
Modify Article 4, Payment of Bills, sections one and two, adding 'subject to the provisions of applicable law' to the shutoff clause

budget_items.topic: Baseline cost for PFAS/iron-manganese treatment plant and transmission mains
budget_items.what_was_said: The board set a baseline construction estimate combining the Hickory Hills SRF-funded portion and the Keings project, to be presented as a single combined vote for residents.

budget_items.topic: SRF vs. bond interest rates for the two project components
budget_items.what_was_said: Commissioners discussed borrowing the larger Hickory Hills/Lancaster portion under the SRF at one rate and financing the smaller Keings portion separately at a higher rate.

budget_items.topic: SRF principal forgiveness and possible emerging-contaminant grant
budget_items.what_was_said: The board debated whether a percentage of principal forgiveness applies automatically under the SRF application, and whether a separate emerging-contaminants grant pool might add further funding; they agreed to seek clarity.

budget_items.topic: Engineering design-services line within the SRF application
budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner calculated that the budgeted design-services fee, at an assumed hourly engineer rate, implied an unreasonably large number of full-time-equivalent engineer-years, arguing the true design cost is much lower; another commissioner noted the figure is the maximum SRF allows, not the actual cost.
The same commissioner compared the budgeted construction-oversight fee to what one engineer working the full construction period at an hourly rate would cost, arguing a large gap between the two.

budget_items.topic: Capital cost per gallon of treatment capacity, compared nationally
budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner presented national cost data for similar-sized PFAS and iron/manganese treatment plants and argued the district's estimated building cost is several times higher than comparable plants elsewhere.

budget_items.topic: Residential vs. commercial water-use figures behind the cost allocation
budget_items.what_was_said: The clerk/treasurer explained a spreadsheet used for the annual statistical report that breaks down usage by connection type, used to check the numbers behind the funding slides.

budget_items.topic: Cost of the Keings-to-Lancaster transmission main
budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner noted the transmission-line cost estimate has varied widely across different reports and design assumptions (pipe diameter), and said the true number awaits final design.

budget_items.topic: Total project cost and impact on resident water bills
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident said the plant, financing and operating costs over the loan term would roughly triple a typical household's annual water bill, and warned many customers are already behind on payments.

budget_items.topic: Delinquent accounts and collections behind new shutoff rule
budget_items.what_was_said: The clerk described the number of bills sent, second notices issued, and accounts running behind, used to justify adding formal payment-plan and shutoff language to the rules and regulations.

budget_items.topic: Resident survey response rate on funding options
budget_items.what_was_said: The board noted only a small share of water takers had responded to the survey and decided to extend the deadline and publicize it further before the special meeting vote.

decisions.decision: A commissioner will draft a letter to MassDEP requesting a variance to allow the Woodland Condo Association's kayak rack to remain, to be reviewed by the absent third commissioner and voted on at a future meeting.

The two commissioners agreed to merge their separate PowerPoint drafts into one combined presentation on PFAS/water treatment funding options, using one commissioner's visual diagram and the other's cost detail.
The board agreed to hold a public presentation at town hall, recorded for local TV, ahead of the special meeting vote.
Extend the resident funding-options survey a couple more weeks and promote it via social media before closing it.

Clarified that the planned SRF/bond vote authorizes funding for the Hickory Hills-to-Lancaster plant and transmission main and, separately at a different rate, the Keings transmission main, and either portion could later be declined if not needed.
Agreed to add discussion of the board's own agenda-item process to the next meeting's agenda.

what_happened.line: Commissioners remained split on locking in the SRF loan for the PFAS plant now versus waiting for firmer design-stage costs, and took no vote on it.
The board voted to hold a special resident meeting in late May, choosing between two possible dates depending on school-space availability.
The board voted to amend the water district's payment-of-bills rules, adding a legal-provisions clause to the shutoff procedure.
The board agreed to send a letter seeking a state variance for a condo association's kayak rack, pending review by the absent third commissioner.
A resident told the board many water customers are already behind on payments and warned the project would substantially raise bills.

why_it_matters: Residents will be asked in late May to vote on how to fund the PFAS/iron-manganese treatment plant -- a loan or a bond -- and that choice sets what shows up on future water bills.
The amended shutoff and collections rule changes how the district handles accounts that fall behind, which matters given commissioners' own count of delinquent accounts.
Whether the district locks in loan funding before or after final design costs are known affects how firm the number residents vote on in May actually is.
